q Mat.7.a7.* Luc.13.32.r Luc.19.9.Infidelem Christus (quo quid abiectius)q Canem appellat ; Herodem item * Vulpem : Fidelem verò, honoris caussa,r filium Abrahæ nuncupat ; Iudas etiam quùm iam Apostolus erat, quia tamen tantùm nomine tenùs Christianusf, Diabolus dicebatur: quanquam quiuis verè sanctus, laicus licet, inter Eos numeratur, qui hujusmodi Regni coelestis hæredes censentur,ε quibus mundus non est dignus: quales diuinus noster Rhetor Chrysostomus dixit, dùm sacris mysterijs interfuit, quodammodò ad coelum rapi. "An censes te (inquit) in terris confistere ? annon potius euectigiò in coelos transferri ? Quod non multùm abludit ab illo Apoc. 1. Reges nos fecit, & Sacerdotes Deo. An quia vir verè Christianus infidelem & impium non minùs quàm Spiritus carnem, coelum terram, filius camem, hæres æternæ gloriæ Diabolum nobilitate & dignitate spirituali superat ; ideone quis virum Sanctum quaelibet cuiuis Regi non sancto, aut Imperatori Ethnico honore ciuili præferendum esse duxerit ? Tantum abest vt præcellentia ordinis, aut potestatis Spiritualis, ex respectu præstantiæ obiecti aut finis, aliquam, inferat præcedentiam ciuilis honoris aut authoritatis super Eos,qui in politico regimine Supremi constituti sunt.

page.notes: Margin note marks: the q, *, r, f marks are clear; the mark before the Hebrew reference is read as ε with doubt, and the reference "Hebr.2.;8." is uncertain (possibly "Hebr.2.3,8."). The bullet mark before "Chrysost.l.3. de Sacerd." is uncertain, and the note itself was not transcribed, because it stands beside the line "An censes te" and I could not confirm its exact position. The "Sacr. X." note beside the heading is uncertain. The ⌣ marks before Ptolomæum, Archimedi, Alexandrum and Aristoteli are unclear printer's signs. The large initial D of "DEindèiure" is joined to the word as the rule requires. The "Aduer-" at the end of the page is a half word and is kept as printed. The Google digitiser stamp at lower right is excluded.
